title: Payment flow variants: authorization, upfront, escrow
caption: extra.paymentFlow decides when money moves relative to the handler. Authorization puts the risk of a failed settle on the seller, upfront puts the risk of a failed handler on the buyer, and escrow holds funds first and charges the real amount after. At least one check always runs before the handler.
alt: Three rows. Authorization, the default: POST /verify, which is read only, then the handler runs, then POST /settle, then 200 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Upfront: POST /settle, then the handler runs, then 200 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Escrow: POST /settle to place a deposit or hold, then the handler runs, then a second POST /settle for the final charge, capture or void, then 200 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.

sourceOfTruth.label: x402 specification v2, section 6.1 Payment Flow Models
